card.name: A two‑storey, 792 × 823 cm
card.summary: A two‑storey, 792 × 823 cm home with a pointy gable roof, white shingle siding, and a bold red front door, arranged in a classic 1920s bungalow plan.
card.description: The house occupies a compact 792 cm × 823 cm footprint and rises two storeys to a striking pointy gable roof that peaks 200 cm above the second‑floor ceiling. A crisp white exterior is clad in traditional wood shingles, while the front entry is highlighted by a solid red door, 90 cm wide and 210 cm tall, set in a timber‑framed façade. Inside, the layout follows a classic 1920s bungalow plan: a welcoming living room, a functional kitchen with built‑in cabinetry, a sun‑room on the second floor, three well‑proportioned bedrooms, and two full bathrooms. The interior walls are timber studs sheathed with drywall, finished in a light plaster. Oak hardwood floors run throughout both levels, and the staircase, with 100 cm wide timber treads, provides a graceful ascent to the upper floor. Eight double‑hung windows, each 120 cm × 150 cm, admit abundant natural light. A modest front porch of 300 cm × 200 cm offers a shaded welcome, capped by its own gable roof. All services—electrical panel, plumbing, HVAC, and insulation—are integrated within the wall cavities, delivering modern comfort while preserving the historic aesthetic.
plan: Measure the lot dimensions (792 cm wide by 823 cm deep) and confirm setbacks, utilities, and zoning for a two‑storey, pointy‑roof house.
Draft a floor plan showing a front entry with a red door, a living room, kitchen, dining area, three bedrooms, two bathrooms, and a sun‑room on the second floor.
Create structural drawings for foundation, floor joists, wall framing, roof trusses and a gable roof with a steep pitch, then obtain building permits.
Coordinate trades: pour concrete slab, frame walls and roof, install roofing shingles, windows, doors, and interior finishes.
Run electrical, plumbing and HVAC rough‑ins, then finish drywall, flooring, paint and install fixtures.
Inspect the completed house, test all doors, windows and systems, and hand over the keys to the owner.
assumptions: Because the brief gave no storey count, the design adopts the two‑storey configuration of the Douglas reference.
Room count follows the Douglas pattern: six rooms total (living, kitchen, dining, three bedrooms) plus a sun‑room, giving three bedrooms and two bathrooms.
A modest front porch is added as a typical feature of the era, measuring 300 cm × 200 cm.
No garage is specified; the design therefore omits a garage, matching the referenced plans that also lack one.
questions: Would you like the roof covering to be asphalt shingles as in the Douglas reference, or do you prefer another material such as slate or metal?
Do you require any specific interior finishes (e.g., hardwood vs. carpet, plaster vs. drywall) beyond the standard 1920s bungalow style?
Is a driveway or any external utility connection (septic, well) needed, and if so, what dimensions or locations are preferred?

card.summary: A two‑storey white clapboard home with a pointy gable roof, red front door, and a large silver refrigerator.
card.description: The residence presents a dignified New England colonial silhouette, its two‑storey white clapboard façade capped by a sharply pitched gable roof of asphalt shingles that draws the eye upward. A bold red front door, framed in solid wood and set on a wide stone threshold, provides a welcoming focal point against the crisp exterior. The house measures 13.26 m wide by 9.75 m deep, offering a generous 1326 cm × 975 cm footprint. Inside, six well‑proportioned rooms—including a sun‑parlor that bathes in natural light—are arranged around a central staircase that climbs 2.74 m on the first floor and 2.44 m on the second. The interior walls are finished in smooth gypsum drywall, painted a soft ivory, while the floors are hardwood on the main levels and tile in the bathrooms. A spacious front porch, 2 m deep, runs the full width of the house, edged by a wooden railing. An attached two‑car garage sits to the side, its sliding metal door matching the house’s functional rhythm. The kitchen is equipped with a large stainless‑steel refrigerator, custom cabinets, and a classic farmhouse sink, all ready for modern living. Every element, from the pointy roof to the red door, respects the 1920s pattern‑book inspiration while delivering contemporary comfort.

Draft a full‑scale site plan and floor‑by‑floor layout, locating the red front door, sun parlor, and garage.

Coordinate MEP engineers to route plumbing, electrical, and HVAC through the walls and service shafts.
Order all building materials, schedule trades for foundation, framing, roofing, and interior finishes.
Finish the interior, paint the exterior white, install the red door, and conduct a final inspection.
assumptions: A two‑car attached garage is provided on the side of the house, as the brief did not specify garage size.
A front porch 200 cm deep extending the full width of the façade is assumed to give the house a welcoming street presence.
Interior finishes are assumed to be standard drywall and hardwood flooring, typical of 1920s pattern‑book homes.
The kitchen includes a standard suite of appliances (range, sink, dishwasher) in addition to the requested large silver refrigerator.

Do you require any specific energy‑efficiency standards or HVAC system type for this home?

card.summary: A two‑storey white‑brick home with a pointy gable roof, red front door, and a kitchen equipped with a large silver fridge, stove, and sink.
card.description: The residence rises two stories on a solid concrete slab measuring 1350 cm by 950 cm, its white brick façade capped by a sharply pointed gable roof of asphalt shingles that commands the streetscape. A bold red wooden front door, hinged and painted to a vivid scarlet, invites guests through a symmetrical elevation punctuated by ten operable sliding windows. Inside, three spacious bedrooms, a sun‑filled parlor, and a formal living area are arranged around a central hallway, each interior wall sheathed in smooth plasterboard. The kitchen, positioned on the ground floor, hosts a large silver refrigerator, a stainless‑steel stove placed immediately to its left, and a matching sink, all fed by concealed plumbing and a dedicated electrical circuit. A two‑car garage occupies the left wing, its steel roll‑up door sliding effortlessly. A welcoming front porch of timber decking extends 300 cm by 200 cm, providing a shaded transition from the sidewalk to the entry. The house is finished with a full set of interior doors, a staircase of timber treads, and a skylight over the sun parlor, delivering natural light to the upper level. Every element respects the proportional language of the 1920s pattern‑book while embracing modern amenities.

Draft floor plans and elevations, incorporating a pointy gable roof and a red front door.
Obtain building permits and coordinate structural, mechanical, and electrical engineers for the two‑storey layout.
Excavate the site and pour a concrete foundation slab sized to the 1350 cm × 950 cm footprint.
Frame exterior and interior walls, install roof trusses, and cover the roof with asphalt shingles.
Install doors, windows, interior finishes, and the kitchen suite consisting of a big silver refrigerator, a stove next to it, and a sink.
Perform final inspections, paint the front door bright red, and hand over the completed home.
assumptions: Because the brief did not specify the number of bedrooms, a typical three‑bedroom layout was chosen to match the six‑room reference plans.
Exterior wall material was assumed to be brick with a white finish, a common choice for 1920s colonial‑style homes.
A front porch was added as a standard feature of the referenced designs, providing a transitional space and visual balance.
The garage was sized for two cars, reflecting the common provision in the reference designs and allowing adequate driveway width.

Do you require any specific interior finishes (flooring, paint colors) beyond the red front door and white brick exterior?
